result:
Nothing is built yet: the package is a greeting `main()` and two smoke tests. So I'm staging this as a new project. The brief is your own words, so its outcomes are the source. The three research reports are background only: I use them for facts, options and costs, and nothing below comes only from them.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision size over time at each of the four stages (first→second, second→third, third→benchmark, post-benchmark/wedge-back), for total nonfarm, from real archived vintages | Small data. Total nonfarm SA and NSA is about 2 series, so a handful of ALFRED calls at the published 120 requests/min limit. Vintage depth is unconfirmed; a probe would settle it |
| O2 | The same by NAICS supersector | About 13 supersectors × SA/NSA, so roughly 26 series. Whether ALFRED holds supersector vintages back far enough is unknown. If not, they must be hand-built from archived releases, and that cost can't be estimated yet |
| O3 | Split of each SA revision into its NSA sample part and its seasonal-factor part, from NSA and SA vintages together | Reuses O1/O2 data, so little extra cost |
| O4 | The effect of collection interval (collection days, placement of the 12th, first-closing rate) on the size of the one-month revision | Collection days follow from release calendars, which is cheap. I don't know how far back published first-closing rates go; the core stage would find out |
| O5 | The effect of slow-moving capacity factors (real appropriations, FTE, sample size, shutdowns/CRs) on revision size, with honest shrinkage and a statement of what isn't identified | Mostly your time: about 45 fiscal years of budget justifications plus FedScope, all transcribed by hand. A firm estimate needs one document opened first |
| O6 | Separate news and noise shares for each revision stage, from a latent-truth multi-vintage model with the benchmark as an irregular, higher-precision observation | Compute can't be estimated without a run. About 550 months × 4 stages; the core stage would measure it |
| O7 | O6 extended: covariates in a Student-t log-scale with stochastic volatility, partial pooling across supersectors, and regimes for 2003 and 2020–22 | Can't be estimated until O6 has run |

The brief's Parts A and B (literature review, gap table, bibliography) are already delivered by the three reports, so I haven't listed them. Tell me if you want a reconciled version as an outcome.

## Proposed tracks

- **A — Revision record** (O1, O2): known progression, total nonfarm first, then supersectors.
- **B — Seasonal vs. sample** (O3): split from A because the share of revisions that is seasonal-factor revision stands without the magnitude record's trend story, and vice versa. Proposed as research; tell me if you consider the decomposition settled arithmetic.
- **C — Collection interval** (O4): research.
- **D — Institutional capacity** (O5): research. Split from C because the two questions are unrelated even though both explain revision size. C uses sharp within-year variation; D uses slow, collinear trends. Joined, C would wait on D's hand-built covariates and its weak identification.
- **E — Latent-truth model** (O6, O7): research. The brief puts C and D inside this model. Splitting them lets their answers arrive without waiting on the full state-space machinery. E can take them in later as covariates.

A–E all read the vintage panel that A's core stage produces, so that dependency comes first regardless of ranking.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv, pytest and ruff (repo).
- NumPyro/NUTS, Dynamax, Blackjax only if needed, ArviZ and Polars (brief). One thing to check: whether JAX wheels exist for 3.14.

## Proposed name

`ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file with that name exists yet.

## Optional probe

With your yes, I'd fetch PAYEMS's full ALFRED vintage history and check one supersector series. That settles the vintage depth and data volume behind O1 and O2. It needs a FRED API key.

**One request:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves. Also confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name, and say yes or no to the probe.
